dispute_evidence.claim: test/series.test.ts's AC-16 test "reads each series with its open occurrence id, or null once it closes" asserts at line 265 that after POST /api/tasks/:id/complete closes a series' open occurrence, GET /api/series/:id reports openOccurrenceId: null. The test's own header comment at lines 259-260 states this as a Phase-2-only assumption: "Once the open occurrence closes, GET reports no open occurrence -- the spawn of a successor is Phase 3's concern (PRD AC-19), out of scope here." PRD AC-19, which phase 3 implements, requires that completing an open occurrence of an active series spawns exactly one new open occurrence in the SAME atomic write. Once that successor exists, findOpenOccurrenceId (src/worker/routes/series.ts:41-50, unmodified by this phase) correctly reports the successor's id, so openOccurrenceId is structurally non-null immediately after such a completion. AC-16 itself only promises "their current open occurrence id (or null)", satisfied either way -- so the contradiction is between this specific phase-2 test assertion, written and approved before AC-19's code existed, and AC-19's now-implemented requirement. npm test fails at exactly this one assertion (1052/1053 passing, expected null, received the successor's real id), with test/tasks.test.ts's own 24/24 AC-19..AC-25 cases green.
dispute_evidence.proposed_resolution: Amend test/series.test.ts:259-265 to assert openOccurrenceId equals the successor spawned by the same POST .../complete call (available from that response's additive successor.id field per AC-19) instead of null, and update the stale comment. If the null-after-complete behavior is judged load-bearing for a reason not captured in the PRD, the alternative is a dated amendment to AC-16 or AC-19 with the owner's confirmation -- the path this PRD's Decisions Log already used once for AC-5.
